key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions including lab abnormalities (all grades, incidence >=20%) were glucose increased, creatinine increased, diarrhea, rash, lymphocyte count decreased, GGT increased, nausea, ALT increased, and fatigue. Serious risks include severe hypersensitivity (including anaphylaxis), severe cutaneous reactions (SJS/EM), hyperglycemia, pneumonitis, and diarrhea. Grade 3 diarrhea occurred in 7% of patients.

citations.quote: Most common adverse reactions including laboratory abnormalities (all grades, incidence ≥ 20%) were glucose increased, creatinine increased, diarrhea, rash, lymphocyte count decreased, GGT increased, nausea, ALT increased, fatigue, hemoglobin decreased, lipase increased, decreased appetite, stomatitis, vomiting, weight decreased, calcium decreased, glucose decreased, aPTT prolonged, and alopecia.

Severe hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis and anaphylactic shock, were reported in patients treated with PIQRAY. Severe hypersensitivity reactions were manifested by symptoms including, but not limited to, dyspnea, flushing, rash, fever, or tachycardia.

Severe diarrhea, including dehydration and acute kidney injury, occurred in patients treated with PIQRAY. Most patients (58%) experienced diarrhea during treatment with PIQRAY. Grade 3 diarrhea occurred in 7% (n = 19) of patients. Among patients with Grade 2 or 3 diarrhea (n = 71), the median time to onset was 46 days (range: 1 to 442 days).

detail.text: Patient selection based on PIK3CA mutations detected by an FDA-approved test; in SOLAR-1 PIK3CA mutations were confirmed using the therascreen PIK3CA RGQ PCR Kit.

requirement.text: Conduct a clinical trial to evaluate the effect of repeat doses of a strong CYP3A4 inducer on the pharmacokinetics of alpelisib and to determine appropriate dosing recommendations.
